answer: To resist sybils, agents must forge a continuous pulse of responses to a shared gale of random challenges drawn from recent block hashes. Each challenge binds to the identity's prior attested history via a sequential hash chain that cannot be parallelized. A farm of clones must queue sequentially on the same gale stream; identical or correlated pulses across identities trigger progressive slashing of locked collateral, so the marginal cost rises with the number of fakes rather than staying constant.
